nodes.description: Address of the contract owner stored in Ownable; controls privileged access.
Constructor of Ownable that assigns owner = msg.sender at deployment time.
Modifier onlyOwner that requires msg.sender == owner before allowing the guarded function body to run.
Owner-only function that validates newOwner != address(0), emits OwnershipTransferred and overwrites the owner state variable.
Owner-only function of DistributeETH that loops over _addrs and performs a low-level send of _bals[i] to each address, throwing on failure.
Payable fallback function of DistributeETH that accepts plain ETH transfers.
msg.sender referenced inside the Ownable constructor; becomes the initial owner.
msg.sender compared against owner inside the onlyOwner modifier; the sole access-control check.
Address parameter of transferOwnership that is written into the owner state variable.
Array of recipient addresses passed to distribute and used as send targets.
Array of wei amounts passed to distribute and used as send values.
Loop counter in distribute; its range is bounded by _addrs.length and it is incremented with ++.
Low-level address.send() external call executed inside the distribute loop; forwards value to an arbitrary address and can trigger recipient code.

edges.reason: The untrusted msg.sender in the constructor is written directly into the owner state variable, making the deployer the privileged account.
The onlyOwner modifier depends entirely on the comparison msg.sender == owner; if owner is wrong or zero the guard is meaningless or permanently blocks callers.
transferOwnership is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier, so ownership changes are gated by msg.sender == owner.
distribute is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier, so only the owner may push funds out of the contract.
newOwner is the sole input parameter consumed by transferOwnership.
The newOwner parameter overwrites the owner state variable, handing full access-control rights to the supplied address.
transferOwnership reads the current owner value to emit the OwnershipTransferred event before reassigning it.
The loop counter i indexes the _addrs array; an unbounded loop over attacker-controlled length can exhaust gas or mis-index.
The loop counter i indexes the _bals array using only _addrs.length as bound, so mismatched array lengths cause out-of-bounds access and revert.
Elements of _addrs are used as the recipient of the low-level send, letting the caller choose arbitrary callee contracts.
Elements of _bals are forwarded as the wei value of the low-level send.
distribute executes the external send inside a loop without updating any state afterwards, so control flow leaves the contract mid-operation.
The recipient of send() can execute its fallback and re-enter distribute before the loop finishes, since no state or reentrancy guard protects the loop.

normalization_plan.reason: newOwner is a pure parameter whose only role is to be assigned into the owner state variable by transferOwnership, so it can be folded into that function node.
_addrs is only consumed by distribute as the send target list and carries no meaning outside that function's execution.
_bals is only consumed by distribute as the value list paired with _addrs and can be merged into the same function node.
The local loop counter i exists solely to drive the low-level send call inside distribute, so it is directly related to and can be normalized into the unsafe_operation node.
